hypoxia upregulates the T‐type Cav3.2 channel gene expression in rat cardiac myocyte, and that this effect requires stabilization of HIF‐alpha, and involves RhoA and Rho kinase I.

the expression of T‐type Cav3.2 Ca2+ channels is induced in cardiac myocytes by hypoxia and that the mechanism underlying this regulation involves the stabilization of the transcription factor HIF‐1, which is required for the activation of the RhoA/ ROCKI signalling pathway.
hypoxia upregulates the mRNA of the T‐channel Cav3.2 in cardiac myocytes by a mechanism involving HIF‐1, RhoA and ROCKI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of Ca2+ channels, and their involvement in the development of arrhythmias and other pathological conditions.
the role of the T‐channel in the development of arrhythmias in ischemic situations.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of T‐type calcium channels in the cardiac muscle.

HIF‐1 is a key regulator of the hypoxic response in cardiomyocytes, and is involved in the re‐expression of T‐type calcium channels in adult cardiomyocyte under hypoxic conditions.
hypoxia upregulates Cav3.2 expression through the stabilization of HIF‐α, and that the HIF‐α/RhoA/ROK signalling pathway is involved in the regulation of the Cav channels.
hypoxic induction of T type Ca2+ channels is an important factor in the development of arrhythmias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF‐1alpha stabilization is a key event in the upregulation and activation of T‐type Cav3.2 calcium channels in cardiac myocytes under hypoxic stress.
the hypoxia‐inducible transcription factor HIF‐1 regulates the expression of T‐type Cav3.2 calcium channels in cardiomyocytes.
the hypoxic induction of Cav3.2 T‐type calcium channels in cardiac myocytes involves the stabilization of HIF‐α proteins and requires the activation of the RhoA/ ROCKI pathway.

the hypoxic induction of T channels is an important factor in cardiac arrhythmias.
